scope: Four functional-NBT variant quest insertion contract and existing consumers. No production repair or native acceptance.

findings.classification: confirmed design-contract ambiguity; not an implemented new-node exploit
findings.title: Personal advancement does not make the FTB node personal
findings.detail: The submitting ServerPlayer supplies the personal advancement check, but progress/completion is keyed by quest/task ID in TeamData selected from the player's current team. Another member of the same party therefore sees the completed FTB task without having crafted. withPlayerContext only tracks the submitter during callbacks; it does not change the progress owner.
findings.required_resolution: Define separate acceptance assertions: only crafter A receives the personal advancement; A/B in one party share FTB completion by normal semantics; B in another team remains incomplete. If personal FTB completion is intended, the present plain advancement-task proposal does not implement it. Do not alter all existing team behavior implicitly.
findings.native_status: Not run; static source confirmation only.

findings.classification: transaction wording and future acceptance gap
findings.title: ItemCraftedEvent fires before crafting-matrix deduction
findings.detail: ResultSlot checks achievements and posts the event, then onTake consumes each ingredient. This is a native crafting-action hook, not a separate post-payment commit event. Normal vanilla control flow subsequently deducts material; this review found no actual free-craft exploit and makes no such claim. Shift-click passes the original pre-transfer copy through Slot.onQuickCraft, so rejecting it as an empty output would be a false alarm.
findings.required_resolution: Do not re-consume ingredients in a future advancement handler. Verify ordinary take, shift-click, full-inventory failure and repeat craft using actual native transactions after authorization; document pre-deduction event timing. Distinguish proof of intended native craft action from crash-safe exactly-once payment settlement.

findings.classification: confirmed identity boundary; proposed handler not yet implemented
findings.title: Registry path alone cannot distinguish these four variants
evidence: Four recipe JSONs and InfusionTraits.java:55-69; ExpansionSupplies.java:20
findings.detail: Both charms reuse ordinary accessory IDs, warm wine reuses marching_wine, and poison smoke uses minecraft:lingering_potion (EquipmentBehaviors.id returns an empty string for this namespace). A future handler routed only through SUPPLIES or the Dynasty-only helper would miss three variants or conflate base items.
findings.required_resolution: Match actual output item plus functional tag(s), independent of translated display Name; validate the active known infusion rather than name text or tag presence alone. Poison requires the vanilla potion item, poison payload and variant marker. A dedicated registered code advancement is required; undefined advancement IDs silently do nothing.

findings.title: Warm-wine crafting also satisfies the legacy marching-wine receipt
findings.detail: A purchased or received base marching wine can be upgraded and the resulting marked wine awards cod4_obtain_marching_wine because it shares the base ID. Thus the old node does not prove the actor personally used the original honey/wolf-fang/red-mushroom recipe. This is existing broad result-based semantics, not a newly introduced reward duplicate.
findings.required_resolution: Preserve completed old advancement/task IDs. Do not reinterpret or reset legacy completion to infer an exact old recipe. New receipt meaning must state whether any functional native result or a particular recipe ID is required.

findings.title: Table infusion is a different transaction from workbench crafting
findings.detail: Table validates owner/current menu/BE/distance/revision, then deducts noncreative material and levels before updating the base and awarding first_infusion. The workbench charm recipes consume two materials, steel and string, not a base claw/plate or XP, and have no jade-table gate.
findings.required_resolution: Do not award workbench craft history from first_infusion, inventory pickup, recipe discovery or purchased items. Keep original workbench path free of the table's get_jade prerequisite.

findings.title: Removing infusion can retain a variant display name
findings.detail: Preview copies the original item and edits/removes only DynastyInfusion; the recipe's custom translated display Name survives removal or replacement. A name-based objective can therefore match a functionally ordinary item through a normal table operation.
findings.required_resolution: Use functional state for current-equipment checks and retain historical craft completion independently. This review does not modify naming behavior.

findings.title: No reward on the five chosen existing predecessor nodes; future rewards need explicit ownership
evidence: Five exact c9 nodes in selected_nodes
findings.detail: All five selected predecessors have rewards:[] and can_repeat:false. Their code advancements have no reward definition. Pack defaults are autoclaim enabled, per-team reward false, linear progression. A future nonempty reward with inherited defaults can be granted to eligible online team members, not only the crafter. Claimed rewards are keyed by reward ID and player/team setting.
findings.required_resolution: Keep proposed nodes rewards:[] and nonrepeatable unless deliberately designed otherwise; preserve old quest/task/reward IDs and do not duplicate automatic payouts in the crafting handler. Repeated crafting alone is not evidence of a duplicate payout.

findings.classification: confirmed boundary for any future use objective; current contract is craft-only
findings.title: Native poison cloud does not retain smoke-variant identity or a simple player-kill receipt
findings.detail: The native throw constructs a projectile from the actual player and consumes one potion outside creative mode. Impact transfers owner, potion effects and fixed color to the cloud, but does not copy cod4PoisonSmoke/display NBT. Poison ticks use generic magic damage only while health>1. A cloud owner or poison effect alone cannot prove use of the marked smoke variant, nor guarantee personal lethal-hit attribution. Hei Po's marked long-poison gu is a separate native merchant result with cod4HeiPoGu, not the workbench smoke recipe.
findings.required_resolution: Keep the proposed task craft-only. Any future paid-use/trade objective needs its own explicit event-boundary review; never count any lingering poison cloud, poison damage or bought gu as personal smoke crafting. No custom projectile system introduced by this review.

findings.classification: confirmed source-of-truth limitation for future insertion
findings.title: Generated chapters and recipe navigation currently lose variant distinctions
findings.detail: recipe_index groups recipes by result registry ID and retains ingredients/count but drops result NBT/display metadata. Current base tiger-claw and scale-plate help consequently describes the variant recipe using the base item name. This does not make existing base-item objectives variant-specific. The supported quest generator rebuilds chapters, so manually adding only the rendered SNBT would not persist on regeneration. All four checked recipe outputs currently agree with their generator formulas.
findings.required_resolution: After the research gate, put dedicated variant objectives and stable IDs in the authoritative quest generation inputs and validate generated output. Preserve base item tasks/rewards. Do not claim variant-specific recipe navigation merely because the base-ID recipe index contains that recipe.

findings.title: Actor binding is present on table requests; repeated awards are guarded, with no duplicate payout demonstrated
findings.detail: Infusion packet takes its sender from server context, checks current container ID, then owner/menu/distance/BE/revision in the menu. BE revision detects changed stacks and invalidates stale previews. Shared table inventory is shared inventory, not proof of who supplied the item. Vanilla advancement reward granting is guarded by newly-completed transition; FTB reward claiming by its existing claim key. Merchant result uses ItemStack.onCraftedBy but does not post Forge ItemCraftedEvent in the inspected native path, so that similarly named callback is not a paid craft receipt.
findings.required_resolution: Keep event sender, actual transaction type and existing claim identities. Do not add a second payout path or manually post crafted events for trades. Preserve party join/leave claimed-reward merging; later runtime tests must distinguish intended per-player rewards from duplicate rewards.
